string.text: Watch out, there’s a pseudodog here!
Thanks for the help.
“Thanks” doesn't put food on the table. If you really want to show your gratitude, answer me one question. \nWord is, you’re looking for Gunslinger. What do you want with him?
Why do you need to know?
Did you two have a falling out?
Wait. Are you Gunslinger?
Well, this is quite the “informative” conversation we’re having — nothing but questions. No, I’m not.
Then what the hell do you want from me?
Oh, just wanted to check something. Never mind. Sorry if my questions bothered you. I bet every stray dog in the Zone is asking you about Gunslinger these days.
Who are you, anyway?

They call me Lone Wolf. Well, see you around. I have a feeling we’ll cross paths again. \nThe Zone is vast, sure, but a stalker’s path always leads toward loot — and where there’s loot, there are other stalkers.
I’ll keep that in mind.
Well?
So?

Hey, Messer. You’ve heard of the Bar, right? They’ve heard of you there too, and they’re actually interested, but you shouldn’t show up at the Bar empty-handed. \nSo, here’s a little tip: there’s a spot in the Dark Valley that might contain the documents the Barkeep is looking for.

It’s a very dangerous place, though. People lose their minds there; their brains get fried. You’ll need a military-grade psi-helmet for protection. \nAs it happens, some special forces troops passed through the Valley recently. Most of them didn’t make it out, but a couple of survivors managed to reach the Garbage.
A stalker mentioned on the network that he saw their camp by a stream near the road to the Valley. Better hurry, before someone else snags those helmets. \nThe Benevolent Lone Wolf.
Hey, Messer, hold up! I’ve been following you all the way from the Garbage.
Wait, Messer, don't drive away! I've been chasing you all the way from the Garbage!
What do you want?
I told you that even though the Zone is vast, we'll meet again, remember? So, how was the Dark Valley?
As if you don't know. Or are you saying you weren't following me?
The good old Messer. Still full of questions.
And with every passing day, there are only more of them.
What are your plans now?
Sleep.
Fair enough, it’s been a rough day. Come on, I’ll show you where you can crash — you’d never find it on your own.
Alright, let’s go. [fast travel]
Alright, let's go.
Here we are. The place is all yours. Get some sleep, and then we’ll head to the bar. We can grab a drink, get a bite to eat, and have a proper talk.
You’re up? Great, let’s head to the bar. I bet you’re dying for a drink, aren’t you?
Well, make yourself comfortable.
So, what was it you wanted to talk to me about?

We’ve only just arrived, and you’re already taking the bull by the horns. By the way, did you hear what happened to Bull? He was leading some greenhorns through the Quiet Hills and ran straight into a pack of bloodsuckers. What a blockhead, why even drag rookies so far North? To use them as scouts to probe for anomalies?
Get to the point.

Just look around—there used to be plenty of people here. Bull and Buffalo — those two hulks were always testing their strength against each other. One’s definitely gone for good, and the other headed off to Bright Beam and never came back. And what about Mope? He’d just sit on his backside, begging the newbies for booze and spinning tall tales about the North. And where is he now?
Doesn't matter. What’s this got to do with me?
You mean you don't know?
Why would I ask then?

In the Zone, people believe in all sorts of things. Some people believe in luck and carry various amulets, or even keep a lucky stalker by their side. Others believe in the material world: money, artifacts, power. Some look to the immaterial, praying to spirits, gods, demons or even to black stones. And then there are those who believe in raw strength, arming themselves with the heaviest guns they can find and banding together into factions.
And what do you believe in?
The truth. The ultimate verity. And I believe, Messer, that you are the one destined to uncover it.
Wait, which one is it? The truth or destiny?

Nothing but questions, as always. I suspect you were a skeptic in your past life. \n\nThere’s a legend that whoever is born three times will be able to reach the heart of the Zone — the place where the whole truth lies hidden. The Death Truck was your second birth; now, only one step remains.

All that’s left is to be "born" a third time. A piece of cake, right? Besides, it’s not like stalkers coming back from the dead is all that rare. Take Doctor, for instance — he’s probably pulling someone "twice-born" back from the beyond every single day.
Doctor… Pulling from the beyond… You’d be surprised. Oh, look. The owner of this establishment has decided to grace us with his presence.
I need to have a word with you about those papers you brought in.
In a rush, are you? Let people enjoy a bit of rest after a job.
Take your rest, but don’t drag it out too long. It’s in your own best interest.
Where would I go?
What’s got him all worked up? And why’d he bring his goons along, too?
The "muscle" got to flex for a bit. Don’t sweat it, Messer. That message wasn’t meant for you.
Then who was it for?

For Rat himself. Who else? You think he’s irreplaceable? Hell no; this is already the fifth one. \n\nAnd being Rat isn’t exactly easy, you know. The last two didn’t even last a month, but this one’s managed to hang on for over six months now. He must be serving someone’s interests quite well.
Okay? But why did he bring those goons along then?
You’re looking at it the wrong way. Maybe it wasn’t Rat who brought them along. Maybe it was them who brought Rat along, eh?
That’s nonsense.
Nonsense or not, I would advise against trusting him. Rat will use you first, then he’ll sell and resell you off. You can’t trust people who aren’t their own masters. Especially here in the Zone.
So, you can be trusted then? If that’s the case, tell me: who do you work for?

Whether I can be trusted or not — that’s for you to decide. I’m an interested party in this, as you can imagine, so my opinion is purely subjective. \n\nBut I can tell you one thing for sure: the Lone Wolf is his own master. And that already sets me apart from many others.
Fine, whatever. I’ll try to get Rat to open up instead.
Give it a shot. I’ll be waiting for you up in the department store; we can discuss whatever Rat tells you then.
If there’ll be anything to discuss, that is.
Leave us alone.
Are you deaf or what?
You’ve got some interesting guards.
Yeah, just great, aren’t they? Morons. Anyway, the documents. Hand them over; I need to look through them, and fast.
What’s the rush?
Because these documents might hold the key to finding a way to the North.
So? Even if we wait another day or two, that key isn’t going anywhere.
Hmm, let’s see… psychotronic emitters, Lake Yantar… Huh? What was that?
Nevermind.

Right, so — these documents mention some kind of psychotronic emitters located in the North. It also says that the research complex at Lake Yantar was responsible for supplying equipment for these emitters. We should pay a visit there.
Go on, then. Off you go. I’ll wait here.
Messer, I’ve told you already. This is in your own interest, too. You’ve heard of the “Black Monolith”, haven’t you?
I have. Fairy tales about the Wish Granter. So, what about it?

At first, I thought they were just typical campfire stories, too. Just people trying to find some justification for the deadly risk that is life in the Zone. \n\nBut when you’re a bartender, you hear a lot of things. Especially when you get to decide who’s allowed into your bar and why. I don’t let blabbermouths in here.
Fine. Let’s say you have my undivided attention.

The Zone is full of abandoned laboratories. You’ve even been to a few yourself. The documents people bring from there lead me to one conclusion: the Zone is, at least partially, man-made. And someone is working very hard to cover up all traces of its human origin. 

Did you hear how Hoplite was taken out? And what about those military expeditions pushing deep into the Zone — clearly searching for something, combing through every single sector? There’s a very important person behind all of this. Or rather, persons — there are some very serious persons behind it. 

I’ve also come across documents that mention a “certain black crystal”. Something that, while perhaps not granting wishes in the literal sense, definitely exerts some kind of influence on the human brain. See where I’m going with this? 

And if someone is going to such great lengths to cover their tracks, it means there’s something real at the heart of it all. But to figure out exactly what, you’d have to reach the very core of the Zone — the sarcophagus of the Chernobyl NPP, which is currently blocked off by the emitters. And if you really are a twice-born, it means you’ve already been on the other side of the “Brain Scorcher” — which also means you can get back there.
As if I’m the only one who’s ever been past the “Scorcher”.
You’re the only one who came back without your brain turned to mush. Sure, you lost your memory, but that’s something you can regain. Unlike your free will or your ability to think clearly.
Which is why you’ve decided to assign the task of going there and making your wish onto me?
I’ll make my own wish; all I need from you is to open the path to it.
And how exactly am I supposed to do that?

Now we’re talking business. Wait a second… Damn, now of all times… This is exactly why you shouldn’t have been sitting around stuffing your face. 

Alright, listen up: start at the Quiet Hills. I’ve heard that the fanatics over at the military base there have dug something up. 

Once you’re done with this, head over to Lake Yantar. You’ll find a scientific camp there—go talk to them. The area around the lake has strong psi-emission, so be careful. 

And here. Take this as a reward for your last job: an artifact transmuter. You can ask the scientists how to use it. 

Alright, get moving, off you go!
Well, well, look at that. Rat has decided to show some initiative, huh? You know as well as I do that the initiative usually ends up biting the initiator.
Greetings, Major. Ahem. Might I suggest we continue this conversation somewhere a bit more private?
And who the hell was that? A military stalker?
The masters have arrived. Looks like Rat won't be playing the rat for much longer.
Were you eavesdropping?
From here? I’m not all-powerful. I was just... snooping. \n\nYou know, you don’t have to dance to Rat’s tune, right? You could always just leave the Zone.
One minute you’re pinning your hopes on me, the next you’re telling me to just walk away. Pray tell, why did you even come to the Zone in the first place?
No real reason. I think I just wanted to prove to myself, and to some other people, that I’m worth something.
Couldn't you have found a better way? Or did your youth just go to your head?
Honestly, I don’t even remember anymore. Life here sort of casts a veil over everything that came before it.
And how do you like the life here?
Well, our life here is, on one hand, rather peculiar, and on the other rather monotonous… It’s not exactly a simple question to answer.
You know, if I were you, I’d give some thought to what you’re doing here and why. And to those other people — the ones you wanted to prove your worth to.
I’ll think about it. And what will you do?
Keep on doing what I’ve been doing; I’ve got nothing to lose. The center of the Zone isn’t the worst goal a person could set for themselves.

In that case, be careful. Plenty of people will try to tail you once you head toward the station. Rat, for starters. \n\nThe center of the Zone is a bit like gold or diamonds — it brings out the worst in people. Wherever there’s even a whisper about the “artifact Klondike” or the “Wish Granter”, you won’t find anything but greed, betrayal, and death.
Same to you. I suppose it’s time for me to go.
Wait. Here. Take my rifle. It helped you out once before, back in the Cordon. Maybe it’ll do the trick again. \n\nTake care, Messer.
